newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers say budget fate linked to own future.
newsitem.headline: India rulers say budget fate linked to own future.

text.p: The fate of India's pathbreaking 1997/98 budget hung in the balance as Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's embattled coalition government kept its options open, party officials said on Friday.
"The fate of the government and the fate of the budget is interlinked," a senior leader of Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The market-friendly budget presented on February 28 was called into question on Sunday after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for Deve Gowda's government.
The lower house of parliament is scheduled to take a confidence vote in Deve Gowda on April 11.
"Passing of the budget is still open," the United Front leader said, adding that the government would convene a meeting of all political parties on the budget if it failed to win the confidence vote.
Newspapers said the budget was sidelined as the government focussed its attention on the trust vote.
"The confidence motion will decide everything. If that is passed, the Finance Bill will not be a problem," Business Standard newspaper quoted Parliamentary Affairs minister Srikanta Jena as saying.
The Finance Bill contains the budget proposals on tax and import tariffs.
Politicians said the budget could still be approved by the parliament after the confidence vote.
"There is a precedent that even after the resignation of the government, the budget has been taken up," speaker P.A. Sangma told reporters at Parliament House on Wednesday.
Industry leaders are keen that the budget, which proposed to slash income tax, corporate tax and import tariffs, should be approved by parliament.
